notes: kb/Work PB5702: COBOL 2002 is judged by its own Annex C.2 (TR 10176:2001), no longer by the 2014 table derived from 2023's Annex B. a) every character of C.2.1 and C.2.2 is an extended letter of the UTF-16 compile-time set (the 2002 repertoire is a subset of the 2014 or 2023 tables, AnnexBCDriftTests). b) the special characters of C.2.1 (U+00B5, U+0559, U+2102 ...) and C.2.2's MIDDLE DOT, and the combining characters (the rows 2014's Annex B.3.1 labels combining, within the 2002 repertoire, because 2002 Annex C labels none), are the medial class: COBOL2773 first or last, accepted inside a word; a character outside Annex C.2 (Syriac, Thaana, Sinhala ...) is COBOL2773. Witnesses at --std 2002: pb5702 accepted test (X, micro sign, y and L, middle dot, L accepted; output ONE TWO) and the refused pb5702 last-in-a-word test (COBOL2773 for Xmicro). c) NOT CONFORMING at 2002 (review finding R1-1): GR4c folds an uppercase extended letter by the Annex D mapping of 2002 (D.2.1 and D.2.2, 600 pairs), but CobolNames.Fold(cp, 2002) is the 2023 Annex C table with Annex E reversed, which holds 86 pairs that 2002 Annex D does not list (measured against specs/ISO_COBOL_2002.md); the Roman numeral pair U+2160/U+2170 is one the reviewer probed: XU+2160Y and XU+2170Y are one item at --std 2002 (COBOL1639) where 2002 has two. The fix is an edition-aware fold: the comparer is the 2023 singleton and the lexer's EditionSpelling can only rewrite a character to the edition's fold, so a 2002 table needs a design (an edition-keyed comparer, or a spelling no table folds); see kb/Work PB5702/2026-11-24-gr4c-fold-is-the-2014-table.md. d) (combining characters count separately in a word's length) is not witnessed by this change, and GR3 above covers only the basic letters.
